summary: Sung-Bae Park is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who completed his doctorate under Lewis Lancaster (~1973–1979). He served as an assistant professor at Dongguk University (~1970–1972) and later became Professor Emeritus at Stony Brook University (post 1977).

Sungdoo Ahn specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen (by 2001). He has served as Director at Geumgang University and Professor at Seoul National University (attested 2013).

Sungtaek Cho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held positions at Stony Brook University and Korea University, serving as Director at Korea University in 2003 and as a professor there (attested 2017).
Sunhee Kim completed a Doctor of Philosophy in Performance Practice at the University of Exeter under the supervision of Phillip B. Zarrilli (attested 2013).

Suniti Kumar Chatterji was an Indologist and linguist educated at Presidency University, University of Calcutta, University of London, and Sorbonne University under Jules Bloch. He held a chair at Calcutta (1922–1952) and served as National Professor in Humanities (~1965–1977).
Supree Kanjanapisarn is a scholar in religious studies and philosophy who completed a PhD at Assumption University under the supervision of Veerachart Nimanong (attested 2011).

Surama Dasgupta was an Indologist and philosopher who completed degrees at the University of Calcutta and the University of Cambridge (PhD 1948), studying under Surendranath Dasgupta. She held a post as Reader in Philosophy at the University of Lucknow.
Surendra Man Bajracharya is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a PhD from Tribhuvan University under doctoral supervisor Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya and co-supervisor Ranjana Bajracharya.

Surendranath Dasgupta was an Indologist and philosopher who earned PhDs from Calcutta and Cambridge, studying under J. M. E. McTaggart. His posts included Principal of Sanskrit College (~1931–1942) and Chair of Philosophy at Calcutta (~1942–1945).

Surya Das is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology practitioner and scholar who studied at the University at Buffalo (~1968–1971) and under the traditional teacher Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje (~1984–1999).

Suryya Kumar Bhuyan was an Indologist and historian educated at Presidency University, Calcutta, and SOAS (PhD 1936). He served as Principal of Cotton University (1918) and later as Vice Chancellor of Gauhati University.
Susan Andrews is a scholar in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Columbia University under the supervision of Chün-fang Yü (attested 2013).
Susan J. Rosenfield is an Indologist who completed her PhD at Harvard University in 2004, studying under faculty including Stephanie W. Jamison and George L. Hart.

Susan L. Beningson is a scholar of art history, archaeology, sinology, and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from Columbia University under the supervision of Robert E. Harrist, Jr. (attested 2009).
Susan L. Huntington is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She held an academic career at Ohio State University (~1971–2011), serving as Professor from ~1986 to 2011.
Susan Meinheit is a Tibetology scholar who held a post at the Library of Congress (attested 1998 and 2007).

Susan Naquin is a historian and sinologist who studied at Stanford and Yale (PhD ~1968–1974). She taught history at the University of Pennsylvania (1977–1993) and served as Professor at Princeton University (1993–2013).

Susan Neiman is a philosopher educated at Harvard (PhD ~1977–1986) and the Free University of Berlin. She held professorships at Yale (1989–1996) and Tel Aviv University (1996–2000), and has served as Director of the Einstein Forum (2000–2026).
Susan Niditch is a religious studies scholar who served on the religion faculty at Amherst College from ~1978 to 2020.

Susan Whitfield is a scholar of sinology, history, and Iranian/Central Asian studies who earned a PhD at SOAS (~1989–1995). She directed the International Dunhuang Project at the British Library (1993–2017) and became Professor at East Anglia (~2018).
